title: coverage_map.json
description: Stage 1 output. The backbone of the honest coverage report and of several auto-weighting defaults. Computed after segmentation; consumed by Stage 2 (pass weighting), Stage 3 (probe weighting), and the user-facing coverage report.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens across all clusters. Very low values mean planning for a reduced-scope core up front.

n_clusters.description: Must equal the length of clusters[] in clusters/manifest.json.

domains.description: Subject areas the corpus actually covers. A single narrow slice means a reduced-scope core.

dialogue_ratio.description: (dialogue + decision_record tokens) / total_tokens. High → raise the interactional pass and probe weight; low → lean on projectible-regularity extraction.

earliest.description: Year of the earliest dated cluster, e.g. '2006'.

latest.description: Year of the latest dated cluster, e.g. '2024'.

gaps.description: Unattested spans, e.g. '2011-2014'. These become explicit caveats in the coverage report.

thin_domains.description: Domains present but under-attested. Must be surfaced in the coverage report — never inside the persona.

n_registers.description: Register families found by Stage 2 Pass A0 (scripts/register_discover.py), mirrored from registers.json. 1 means the distance matrix was computed and supports pooling — a finding, not a default. Read by the Stage 4 cluster-budget formula as +220·max(n_registers-1,0), capped at 3, so a multi-register corpus is granted the room its extra voice work needs instead of being squeezed into a single-voice allowance.

sources.description: One acquisition record per source the corpus was built from. Omit for a purely local corpus; required in practice for anything remote, since it is the only place the retrieval is recorded.

firsthand_ratio.description: Firsthand tokens / total_tokens, from the attribution labels in clusters/manifest.json. A low value is a coverage-report caveat, not a blocker — but the user needs to see it, because it is the number that says how much of this persona came from the person rather than from people writing about them.

type.description: How it was acquired. See acquisition.md for what each one means and how to fetch it.

location.description: Path for local sources; URL for remote ones. For a site, the path prefix that was crawled — never the bare domain.

retrieved.description: ISO 8601 retrieval date. Omit only for local sources.

licence.description: The licence the source publishes under, when it states one. A knowledge base's own licence is binding even when its subject is your subject.

examples.notes: Heavy on monologic prose; little live dialogue. Roughly a third is secondhand reading notes — corroborating only. Three register families; the spoken/written gap is the largest.
